findings.description: Setting strict to false also disables strictNullChecks, which TanStack Router requires. Running the build's tsc -b step now fails at createRouter calls with "strictNullChecks must be enabled in tsconfig.json" and at route params throughout the UI, so validate:types and the production build cannot complete. Restore strict: true (also required by repository rule 11).
findings.failureMode: tsc -b --noEmit and build tsc step fail throughout UI because TanStack Router types reject strictNullChecks disabled
findings.title: Keep strict mode enabled so the UI can type-check

findings.description: For 'Stays in Not Ready', both the work-pool and work-queue editors always write the selected status to expect and never set after. Proactive triggers detect absence of expect, so the initial not-ready event meets the expectation and a resource that remains not-ready does not fire after within expires. Set after to the selected entry status and expect to its exit statuses in proactive mode, clearing after in reactive mode. The same correction is needed in work-queue-status-trigger-fields.tsx:36.
findings.failureMode: Both proactive pool and queue status editors emit absence-of-status triggers instead of stay-in-status triggers, missing alerts after within
findings.title: Encode proactive pool and queue status persistence

findings.description: Select Reactive/Not Ready, switch to 'Stays in', then select Not Ready again. The new binding writes after=['prefect.deployment.not-ready'] but retains expect=['prefect.deployment.not-ready']. If the deployment becomes Ready before within expires, its ready event is ignored, so the trigger fires even though the deployment did not stay Not Ready. When entering proactive status mode, replace expect with the exit-status events instead of retaining the reactive expectation.
findings.failureMode: Reactive Not Ready -> Proactive Not Ready retains same-state expect and fires after deployment has already become Ready
findings.title: Update expectations when switching deployment posture

findings.description: Configure 'Stays in Not Ready', then change posture to 'Enters' and select Ready. The status field now updates expect, but after still contains prefect.deployment.not-ready. Consequently a Ready event cannot start a bucket until a Not Ready event has first been seen, so this reactive trigger misses Ready transitions it should handle. Clear after when switching to Reactive.
findings.failureMode: Proactive Not Ready -> Reactive Ready leaves after not-ready and suppresses Ready events without a prior Not Ready event
findings.title: Clear deployment after events when returning to reactive mode

findings.description: Clearing Expected Events stores [''], because ''.split('\n') always has one entry and the length check never selects undefined. The backend interprets an empty expectation as any event, but [''] matches only the empty event name, so typing and then clearing this optional field makes the custom trigger stop matching real events. Store [] or undefined for empty text while preserving newline editing.
findings.failureMode: Typing then clearing custom expected events serializes expect [''] and matches no real events
findings.title: Clear custom events to an empty list

findings.description: The new proactive Within inputs allow 1–9 seconds (min=0), and EventTriggerSchema accepts those values. For example, 'Stays in' with within=5 passes trigger validation and advances the wizard, but the backend rejects it because proactive windows must be at least 10 seconds. Set the proactive minimum to 10 and enforce it in form validation. This also affects the deployment, work-pool, and work-queue Within inputs.
findings.failureMode: New editors accept proactive within=5 as valid, producing a trigger rejected by the backend validator
findings.title: Enforce the backend's proactive duration minimum

findings.description: A valid number-input value such as 1e2 is converted to 1 by parseInt, so the form emits a threshold of one instead of the requested 100. Use Number(e.target.value), as the other trigger editors do, to preserve the complete numeric value.
findings.failureMode: Entering or pasting 1e2 into work-pool threshold saves 1 instead of 100
findings.title: Parse the entire threshold number

findings.description: FormControl wraps the Radix Select root rather than SelectTrigger, so its generated id and accessibility attributes never reach the combobox button. The Status label consequently points to no control: getByLabelText('Status') fails, and screen readers cannot identify the status dropdown. Move FormControl inside Select around SelectTrigger. The same wrapping error occurs in work-pool-status-trigger-fields.tsx and work-queue-status-trigger-fields.tsx.
findings.failureMode: Status label has no associated control and the three new status comboboxes lack accessible names
findings.title: Attach status labels to the select trigger

Rule 10 requires a same-directory test for every React component; the TriggerStep smoke test does not satisfy that file contract, and running the component-specific test target finds no tests. Add the co-located component test.

findings.title: Add the required co-located custom-trigger test

findings.description: The MagicLink module was not renamed and remains services/lib/magic-link/MagicLink.js. Requiring ../../lib/magic-link/magic-link throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND when the Members API loads, preventing startup. Restore the existing module path until that file is renamed.
findings.failureMode: Members API fails to load on case-sensitive filesystems because MagicLink.js was not renamed.
findings.title: Use the existing MagicLink filename

findings.description: Ghost boot calls emailAnalytics.init(), which now requires ../email-service/email-event-storage. That file does not exist; the storage module remains EmailEventStorage.js. Node throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND and aborts initialization. Restore the existing import until the corresponding file is renamed.
findings.failureMode: Email analytics initialization throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND for email-event-storage.
findings.title: Keep the existing EmailEventStorage module path

findings.description: The processor still exists as EmailEventProcessor.js, so the new ../email-service/email-event-processor import cannot resolve. Even after correcting the storage import on line 12, emailAnalytics.init() throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND here and boot cannot complete. Restore this import to the existing processor filename.
findings.failureMode: Email analytics initialization throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND for email-event-processor independently of the storage import.
findings.title: Keep the existing EmailEventProcessor module path

findings.description: The import edits remove semicolons on lines 1–4 and 6–10. This violates mandatory rule 19 and the Ghost ESLint semi rule, causing lint:server to fail on the Members API file. Restore statement terminators on all nine declarations.
findings.failureMode: Server lint fails for nine new Missing semicolon errors.
findings.title: Restore semicolons on the import declarations

findings.description: services/lib/magic-link still contains MagicLink.js, not magic-link.js. The new require therefore throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND while MembersAPI is loaded through members/api.js, preventing Ghost startup. Restore the import to ../../lib/magic-link/MagicLink.
findings.failureMode: MembersAPI module loading fails with MODULE_NOT_FOUND for magic-link.
findings.title: Keep the MagicLink import matched to its filename

findings.description: The new ../email-service/email-event-storage path does not exist: the module is still named EmailEventStorage.js. Ghost boot calls emailAnalytics.init(), which now throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND and aborts startup. Restore the import to ../email-service/EmailEventStorage.
findings.failureMode: Calling email analytics init throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND at the new email-event-storage require.
findings.title: Restore the EmailEventStorage import path

findings.description: EmailEventProcessor.js was not renamed, so ../email-service/email-event-processor cannot resolve. Even after fixing the preceding storage import, emailAnalytics.init() throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND here and aborts Ghost startup. Restore the import to ../email-service/EmailEventProcessor.

findings.title: Restore the EmailEventProcessor import path

findings.description: The import declarations on lines 1–4 and 6–10 lost their semicolons. The repository's existing ESLint configuration reports nine semi errors, so yarn lint:server fails on this file. Keep the renamed paths but restore the statement terminators required by mandate 19.
findings.failureMode: Existing lint:server command exits nonzero with nine Missing semicolon errors.
findings.title: Restore required semicolons on the imports

findings.description: Disabling strict also disables strictNullChecks, which TanStack Router requires. The configured tsc -b --noEmit check now fails across existing createRouter calls with 'strictNullChecks must be enabled in tsconfig.json' and breaks the build before Vite runs. It also violates rule 11 by weakening type validation. Restore strict: true.
findings.failureMode: validate:types and build fail because TanStack Router's types reject compiling without strictNullChecks.
findings.title: Keep strict mode enabled for the router types

findings.description: The Stays in posture still writes the chosen work-pool status to expect, with no after event. Thus 'Stays in Not Ready for 30 seconds' monitors missing Not Ready transitions rather than residence in Not Ready, and can trigger repeatedly even after the pool becomes Ready. Use the posture-dependent after binding for proactive status triggers, as the deployment component does. The same defect exists in work-queue-status-trigger-fields.tsx:36.
findings.failureMode: Proactive work-pool/work-queue triggers fire on absence of a status event instead of staying in the selected status.
findings.title: Start proactive status timers with after

findings.description: Clearing the textarea stores [""] because split always returns a nonempty array. The backend treats an empty expect set as matching any event, but [""] as a literal empty event name, so a visually empty form instead produces a reactive trigger that never matches. Filter out blank lines and store [] for empty input.
findings.failureMode: An empty custom event field serializes a literal empty event name rather than matching all events.
findings.title: Normalize empty custom event input

findings.description: Pasting a valid number-input value such as 1e3 saves threshold=1 because parseInt stops at the exponent, rather than saving 1000. The resulting work-pool trigger uses a different threshold than the user entered. Use Number(e.target.value), as the other templates do.
findings.failureMode: Scientific-notation threshold accepted by a number input is saved with the wrong integer value.
findings.title: Parse the complete numeric threshold

findings.description: The new Proactive Within inputs allow values 1–9, and EventTriggerSchema also accepts them, so the wizard advances with a trigger that the backend rejects ('within for Proactive triggers must be greater than or equal to 10 seconds'). Enforce that minimum for proactive intervals before advancing. This is repeated in custom-trigger-fields.tsx:79 and both work-pool/work-queue-status-trigger-fields.tsx:95.
findings.failureMode: The new forms accept positive proactive intervals below the backend's minimum and generate invalid event trigger data.
findings.title: Enforce the proactive ten-second minimum

findings.description: FormControl wraps Select's non-DOM root, so its generated id and aria attributes never reach SelectTrigger. The new status combobox therefore has no accessible name or association with the Status label; getByLabelText('Status') fails and screen-reader users cannot identify the field. Wrap SelectTrigger in FormControl instead. The same misplaced wrapper appears in work-pool-status-trigger-fields.tsx:42-43 and work-queue-status-trigger-fields.tsx:42-43.
findings.failureMode: Status controls are unlabeled in the accessibility tree because generated form control props are dropped by Radix Select.Root.
findings.title: Attach the form control props to SelectTrigger
